title: Claiming Capital Gains Tax Exemption on Asset Sales up to ₹10 Crore
description: Selling long-term capital assets like shares, mutual funds, or gold can lead to capital gains tax. Section 54F of the Income Tax Act allows you to exempt thes.

faq.q: What is the difference between Section 54 and Section 54F?
faq.a: Section 54 applies when you sell an existing residential house property and reinvest the capital gains into another residential house. Section 54F applies when you sell *any* long-term capital asset (other than a residential house) and reinvest the *net sale consideration* into a residential house.
Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are eligible to claim exemption under Section 54F, provided they meet all the specified conditions, including reinvesting in a residential house property in India.

faq.q: What happens if I sell the new property within three years?
faq.a: If the new residential property purchased or constructed using Section 54F exemption is sold within three years, the capital gain exempted earlier will be reversed and become taxable in the year of the new property's sale.

faq.q: Is there a maximum limit on the capital gain I can exempt?
faq.a: While there isn't a direct cap on the capital gain itself, for transfers made on or after April 1, 2023, the cost of the new residential house property considered for exemption under Section 54F cannot exceed ₹10 crore. This effectively limits the maximum exemption amount.

faq.q: Can I invest in more than one residential property to claim this exemption?
faq.a: No, the exemption under Section 54F is available only if the investment is made in *one* residential house property in India.

faq.q: What if I can't buy a property before filing my ITR?
faq.a: If you cannot utilise the full amount of the net sale consideration for purchasing or constructing the new residential property before the due date for filing your Income Tax Return, you must deposit the unutilised amount into a Capital Gains Account Scheme (CGAS) with a public sector bank.

faq.q: Do I need to report this exemption in my ITR?
faq.a: Yes, you must report the sale of the original asset, the long-term capital gain, and the claim for exemption under Section 54F in your Income Tax Return for the relevant assessment year.

based_on.title: Sold shares, gold or property? Here's how you can legally claim capital gains tax exemption of up to ₹10 crore
